prompt: The first and most important step in decontamination is

options.text: Cleaning to remove soil/bioburden before disinfection or sterilization
Sterilizing first to kill pathogens, then cleaning the instruments afterward
Soaking in high-level disinfectant to make the instruments safe to handle
Inspecting instruments under magnification for damage and missing parts

explanation: Soil shields microbes from sterilants; cleaning is prerequisite to sterilization.

distractorExplanations.b: Reverses the sequence: sterilant cannot penetrate soil, so cleaning must come before sterilization, not after it.
distractorExplanations.c: HLD soaking is not the first step; organic soil inactivates disinfectants, so manual or mechanical cleaning comes first.
distractorExplanations.d: Magnified inspection happens in prep and pack after cleaning; it is a quality check, not the first decontamination step.

prompt: PPE in decontamination typically includes:

options.text: Cloth scrub top, latex exam gloves, and a surgical mask without eye protection
Fluid-resistant gown, gloves, mask/eye protection, and appropriate footwear controls
Sterile surgical gloves, a bouffant cap, and a sterile gown as worn in the OR
Lab coat, nitrile exam gloves, and safety glasses as used in the prep and pack area

explanation: Decontam is the dirtiest area—dress for splash/sharps hazards.

distractorExplanations.a: Omits eye/face protection and uses a non-fluid-resistant cloth top; decontam splash risk requires fluid-resistant attire and eye protection.
distractorExplanations.c: Sterile OR attire protects the patient, not the worker; decontam needs fluid-resistant, heavy-duty PPE, not sterile gloves and gowns.
distractorExplanations.d: Prep-and-pack attire does not cover splash and sharps hazards; decontam requires fluid-resistant gowns, utility gloves and face protection.

prompt: Manual cleaning scrubbing should be done

options.text: Above the water line under running tap water so soil is visible
Using steel wool or abrasive pads on stainless instruments to remove stains
Below the water line to reduce aerosols, using appropriate brushes
Before soaking, using a high-pressure air gun to blow off visible soil

explanation: Minimize aerosols; select brushes that contact lumens/crevices without damaging devices.

distractorExplanations.a: Brushing above the water line or under running water creates aerosols; scrubbing is done submerged to contain splash.
distractorExplanations.b: Abrasive pads and steel wool scratch the passivation layer and promote corrosion; use soft brushes as the IFU directs.
distractorExplanations.d: Air or water pressure guns blowing off dry soil create aerosols; manual scrubbing is done submerged first, with guns used per IFU.

prompt: Gravity displacement sterilizers remove air by:

options.text: Mechanical vacuum pulses that pull air out of the chamber before steam enters
Steam entering and forcing cooler air out through a drain passively
Steam flush and pressure pulses above atmospheric pressure
Heating the chamber dry first so air expands and vents out

prompt: Steam sterilization efficacy depends heavily on

options.text: Chamber pressure alone, since pressure kills microbes
Time, temperature, and saturated steam contact
Superheated dry steam at the highest possible temperature
Cycle length and the number of chemical indicators used

explanation: Steam sterilization requires adequate sterilant contact under validated parameters. Proper air removal and drying are also part of the designed cycle.

distractorExplanations.a: Pressure is a means to raise steam temperature; microbial kill comes from time at temperature with steam contact.
distractorExplanations.c: Superheated steam behaves like dry heat and sterilizes poorly; saturated steam with proper moisture is required.
distractorExplanations.d: Indicators monitor the process but do not make it effective; efficacy depends on time, temperature and steam contact.

prompt: A biological indicator (BI) is used to:

Challenge the sterilization process with resistant spores to verify lethality
Show that a package was exposed to the sterilization process
Verify that the cleaning process removed protein residue before instruments are packaged

explanation: BIs provide the highest level of sterilization process challenge.

distractorExplanations.c: Exposure is shown by an external chemical indicator; a BI challenges lethality with live spores.
